html:
SMTO-EXE-0122 — SMTO isn't allowed to use that browser profile or folder

GUID: eae5909f-d7ef-587b-adc7-dc60164657c1
Slug: browser-permission-denied
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO tried to open a browser with saved settings, but the folder it would use either belongs to something else or can't be accessed. SMTO didn't change that folder.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO to start a temporary browser session instead of one with saved settings. A temporary browser uses a fresh folder that SMTO creates itself, so this folder conflict can't happen.
  2. If you need sign-ins to be remembered, ask SMTO to use a new saved-profile name it hasn't used before. A new name gives SMTO an empty folder of its own to keep the saved settings in.
  3. Ask the person who manages the Gateway to check that its account can read and write the browser folder, normally .smto/browser in its home folder. SMTO stops if the account running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to work on a computer) can't use that folder.
  4. Don't ask SMTO to use your everyday browser's profile or copy its data. SMTO never takes over another program's browser data, to protect your passwords and sign-ins.

What success looks like

  • SMTO starts the browser and shows its open tabs without this message.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't delete the existing profile folder to get past this; it may hold another program's data or your saved sign-ins.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway refused a browser operation because a persistent profile folder already holds data without SMTO's .smto-owned marker, or a file-system permission error occurred before any browser action.

What this means

  • A persistent profile directory contained existing data without the SMTO ownership marker, or a browser service step raised PermissionError before confirmed effects. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • A persistent profile directory contained existing data without the SMTO ownership marker, or a browser service step raised PermissionError before confirmed effects.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish profile-ownership refusal from ordinary OS access denial; preserve unrelated profile data and existing sessions.

How to fix it

  • PlaywrightBackend._start raises permission_denied when the profile folder under GATEWAY_BROWSER_PROFILE_ROOT/managed (or managed/users/ followed by the workspace ID) is non-empty and lacks .smto-owned; BrowserService maps a pre-effect PermissionError to the same kind. Use an ephemeral session or a new profile name, or make the Gateway's OS account own the profile root (mode 0700). Never point a profile at Chrome/Edge/Firefox data or add the marker to adopt foreign data.
  • Check Gateway filesystem and browser access permissions. Managed profiles must be dedicated SMTO-owned directories.

Retry and execution caution

  • Check Gateway filesystem and browser access permissions. Managed profiles must be dedicated SMTO-owned directories.

How to verify the fix

  • A dedicated owned profile and authorized resources are used without adopting another application's browser data.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
